articleTitle: EEG-ECG Extraction for Wearable All-in-One Healthcare Device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Stroke and ischemic heart conditions are the leading cause of death; thus, they require prompt diagnosis and treatment. Two non-invasive methods with high sensitivity that can aid in early diagnosis are Electroencephalogram (EEG) and Electrocardiogram (ECG). However, traditional measurements are usually performed in hospitals and require multiple electrodes placed at different positions on the body, which is hard to measure and determine your health continuously. Thus a compact wearable device that can measure both ECG and EEG signals is needed. This paper proposes an extracting model called EEG-ECG Extraction (EEE), a combination of Independent Component Analysis (ICA) and Wavelet shrinkage techniques to determine both EEG and ECG at the same time from a single type of bio-electrical signal from a few sensors at the head. The results show that important information such as heart rate, QRS complex, and QT interval can be determined from EEG signals through ECG extraction. The correlation between the extracted and original signals is also used to evaluate the proposed technique.

articleTitle: A New Method for Peer-to-Peer Assisted Fast Channel Zapping in IPTV Multicast System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a FCZ (Fast Channel Zapping) scheme exploiting P2P (Peer-to-Peer) communication in IPTV (Internet Protocol TeleVision) multicast system. In the proposed scheme, STB (Set-Top Box) devices cache its watching channel for P2P delivery, and the session management server collects the viewing information of STB devices managed by the server in real time. STB device trying to change watching channel receives a candidate STB list for P2P connection from the session management server. P2P-connected STB devices among the candidate STB list are selected by considering both their accessibility and available bandwidth. They deliver the minimum amount of caching data to the STB device attempting to change the channel prior to incoming multicast stream of the switching channel, which results in immediate playback. Compared with the FCZ scheme using a caching server, the proposed scheme can achieve faster channel switching without the additional infrastructure.

publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: This study presents a non-invasive blood glucose concentration (BGC) system that is based on the Internet of Things (IoT) and employs near-infrared sensors (NIR) to detect blood glucose levels through the scanning of fingers. The purpose is to develop a BGC system and assess the accuracy of the proposed system. Constant monitoring and data-driven insights for optimum treatment and enhanced quality of life are made possible by IoT-based systems, and non-invasive glucose monitoring is a critical component of diabetes care. The system that was built comprises of a Light Emitting Diode (LED) that emits signals that are sent via the fingertip, and a phototransistor that is positioned next to the LED to detect any reflected signals. The results of the scanning are then stored in ThingSpeak. The technique used to determine the blood glucose level involves analyzing the variation in received signal intensity that results from reflection. Using regression analysis, a mathematical relationship between glucose concentration and voltage was established and installed in the Arduino. Two sorts of testing were carried out to evaluate the system: in vitro tests on glucose solution and in vivo experiments on the human body. By comparing 10 readings acquired from both types of experiments, the results of the studies indicate that the device's glucose detection accuracy ranges from 1.13 to 16.41%. IoT approach is feasible due to its continuous monitoring capabilities, data analysis, and remote access features, making it a promising tool for effective diabetes control.

articleTitle: Non-Linear Model Predictive Speed Control of Six Phase Squirrel Cage Generator in Wind Energy System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Due to the intermittent nature of wind, varying wind speed causes imbalance in the current of the six phase squirrel cage induction generator (SCIG). These changes in the input signal create inbalance in the current and therefore causes deviations in the torque and flux of the generator. Therefore, this work develops non-linear model predictive control (NMPC) scheme for the generator to ensure that uncertainties in the input of the wind energy conversion system (WECS) have little effect in the quality of output power supplied to the grid. Simulation results obtained when NMPC technique was used in controlling the generator in the WECS showed the effectiveness of the aforementioned technique. The results obtained from the developed scheme were compared with those obtained when backstepping controller was used in controlling the six phase SCIG. It was observed that the developed scheme outperformed the backstepping technique in terms of electromagnetic torque by 16.844%, while a 61.1% improvement was observed in terms of settling time for the rotor flux of the developed technique over that of the backstepping. Finally, the results obtained for the DC link voltage output showed an improvement in terms of overshoot and settling time respectively.

Author Keywords: six phase squirrel cage induction generator

articleTitle: Replay Attack in TLS 1.3 0-RTT Handshake: Countermeasure Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Transport Layer Security (TLS) is an Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) standard protocol commonly used on the Internet nowadays. TLS 1.3 the latest version published in August 2018 introduced a new mode to perform the handshake in zero round-trip time (0-RTT) which led to a significant improvement in the protocol performance. 0-RTT handshake mode allows the client to establish the connection and send the application data in the first message (ClientHello) without waiting for the server to send a response. But it also opens a window for replay attacks. The attack occurs when a valid 0-RTT handshake message is captured and sent again to the server causing the server to perform the same process again according to the application data carried in the message. Several anti-replay protection techniques were introduced to prevent or mitigate the replay attack. This paper sheds light on replay attacks countermeasures for TLS 1.3 0-RTT handshake mode and the most recent proposed methods. The strength and limitations of these countermeasures are discussed. In addition, the paper deliberates on the challenges such countermeasures impose in a distributed environment, for instance, multiple servers in a cloud computing environment or a content delivery network (CDN).

articleTitle: Underwater Brushless Motor Performance Analysis of Twin Hull-based Unmanned Surface Vehicle for Water Quality Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)

authors.preferredName: Tun Khairin Aiman Tun Mohd Khairi

abstract: Unmanned Surface Vehicle (USV) has been used in many applications for environmental surveying, maritime patrolling, and performing specific tasks such as hydrological parameters measurement. The selection of the types of USVs is important as it determines their speed profile and stability while maneuvering on the water's surface. Therefore, the twin hull-type USV is studied in this work, and the suitable thruster is computed and determined to provide a stable USV platform with a low-cost propeller system. The total buoyancy weight of the designed USV is also calculated so that it will be partially immersed in the water in real deployment later. It is important to determine the propeller type to move the USV carefully. The thruster is chosen to be double the total weight of the USV. The performance of the twin hull-type USV again air resistance is performed, and the result shows no air turbulence generated. The total weight of the USV is about 6kg, and the total thruster of the propeller is 13.6 kgf. Based on the result, two types of propellers' frequencies have been tested, 88 and 22 KHz, for the air and water. It is found that, for 88 KHz, the output voltage of the propeller is gradually changed from 2.37V to 14.00V when tested in the air. While on the other hand, the 22 kHz, the output voltage is changed from 0v to 4.1v when tested in air. However, the velocity becomes stagnant when the propeller is tested in the water. In conclusion, the results show that the designed USV provides the necessary information for future real-time deployment and autonomous navigation.

articleTitle: Rank-based Contents Caching and Distribution Scheme for Resource-Efficient Fast Channel Zapping in IPTV Service
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a rank-based contents caching and distribution scheme of caching channels in FCZ (Fast Channel Zapping) cache servers. Cache servers store certain amount of recent multicast streams including intra frame for all channels and serve cached data at high speed in unicast stream while a set-top box requests cached data regarding the newly joined multicast stream on channel change. The set-top box can achieve the fast channel change by reassembling the cached data only with a small amount of multicast stream reception for new channel. However, most of channels under caching in a cache server have not been chosen because channel change toward non-popular channels rarely happens. We address here how caching channels are efficiently distributed over cache servers in server's resource point of view. Since viewer rating of IPTV channels is biased to a few popular channels, cache servers can take channel popularity into consideration for optimizing overall resource utilization. The proposed scheme classifies IPTV channels into two groups, popular channel group and non-popular channel group, based on popularity rank. Each cache server is then assigned to the appropriate channel group, which not only saves its resources by caching the data from its assigned channel, but also improves serviceability (the number of concurrent FCZ sessions), i.e., not necessary caching all the channels alone. Test results prove superiority of the proposed scheme in terms of the total number of concurrent FCZ sessions.

articleTitle: Design of 4-Channel Multiplexer Using Waveguide Cylindrical Cavity Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: The design of a 4-channel multiplexer using a waveguide cylindrical cavity resonator of second order and fourth order is presented in this paper. The performance of the multiplexer is improved when implementing the higher order. The proposed multiplexer design is based on a manifold structure that uses a TE011 mode resonator as the filter channel element. The design procedure involves the use of FD3D and FEST 3D of CST Microwave Studio software to optimize the dimensions of the resonator and waveguide sections to achieve the desired performance parameters, such as insertion loss, return loss, and isolation. The simulated results show that the proposed multiplexer design achieves good performance by featuring the insertion loss is less than 1 dB, and the return loss is better than 10 dB over the 10 GHz band. The isolation between the channels is more than 10 dB, which is suitable for most applications. The proposed multiplexer design is simple, compact, and has good performance characteristics, making it suitable for use in various microwave applications.

articleTitle: Water Quality Monitoring System Based on the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: People's lives always necessitate prioritizing having the best possible and accessible water quality. Since pollution sources continuously expand, water quality monitoring systems have become essential. However, such monitoring systems remain too expensive. Fortunately, with the recent growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) technology and the ongoing development of smart monitoring systems, a low-cost smart water quality monitoring system can be implemented. This paper presents a novel methodology for water quality monitoring systems, allowing smart acquisition of water data, real-time monitoring, and the maintenance of the optimal water quality required for the intended audience. This work provides the necessary monitoring options in a reliable and cost-efficient manner. The system design consisting of hardware and software architectures is presented and investigated.

articleTitle: Onset Estimation of Delayed Cerebral Ischemia by Detecting Change Points in a Time Series of Heart Rate Variability Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Predicting the severity of patient illness and the risk of sudden change, as well as early detection and seamless response in the event of such an occurrence, are important life-or-death issues in the medical field. Many attempts have been made to address this issue in intensive care units/high care units <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{ICUs}/\text{HCUs})$</tex>, including risk assessment at the time of admission using prognostic scores and constructing an artificial intelligence-based rapid-change prediction system based on data collected from life support systems. We investigated the estimation of delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) onset, a prognostic complication, based on continuous heart rate variability (HRV) monitoring for approximately 2 weeks and offline change point analysis of 22 HRV parameter time series for five patients admitted to an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{ICU}/\text{RCU}$</tex> with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{aSAH})$</tex> due to ruptured cerebral arteries and who underwent surgical treatment. Common change points were detected simultaneously for several HRV parameters, and common change points were observed within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 1$</tex> day of the estimated time of onset of DCI in four patients. Thus, continuous HRV monitoring and online analysis of HRV parameter time series suggested the possibility of the early detection of DCI, a complication that greatly affects patient prognosis.

articleTitle: TCM Tongue Segmentation and Analysis with a Mobile Device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Mobile devices and applications provide increased accessibility to things like Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM). Ideally, one would be able to seek out a diagnosis to the tongue using advanced machine learning models in a mobile device. However, such kind of models are still not yet available for the public. In this research, we investigated a way of combining machine learning with a mobile application to support tongue diagnosis for the public. For tongue segmentation, we experimented with an unsupervised approach (K-means), a supervised method and a deep learning model. There are two outcomes presented in this research. Firstly, the user can seamlessly take a picture from a mobile phone and send it over to the server for a segmentation process. Secondly, the image processed by the server would have at least some levels of autonomous analysis preformed on it with acceptable results using machine learning methods. Our current results indicate that we were able to finish some key steps in this process.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Hand Functions Using Sensor-Based Wearable Hand Motion Analysis Device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 6th International Conference on Electrical, Electronics and System Engineering (ICEESE)
abstract: Achieving accurate and quantitative evaluation of hand functions is essential for effective rehabilitation and training programs. This study aimed to develop a lightweight wearable hand motion analysis device utilizing Inertial Measuring Units (IMU) and Force Sensing Resistor (FSR) technology. The device was designed to enhance conventional qualitative evaluation procedures by providing objective and quantitative data. Validation was achieved by investigating the impact of handedness, gender, and exercise habits on finger active range of motion and fingertip force production using the prototype developed. A total of 12 subjects of similar age group were recruited. The subjects' handedness, gender, and exercise habits were recorded, and their hand grip strength, finger active range of motion, and fingertip force production were measured. The analysis revealed significant differences between left- and right-handed individuals, particularly in the flexion of the right index and middle fingers. However, no significant difference in fingertip force exertion was observed between the hands. Additionally, gender-based differences were found in the angular extension and flexion of all fingers, with significant differences observed primarily in extension movements. Fingertip force varied significantly for all fingers, except the left middle finger. These findings indicate that hand dominance, gender, and exercise habits have varying degrees of influence on hand function. Quantitative data on the factors that affect finger range of motion and fingertip force production were successfully derived and analyzed using the developed prototype. This could be useful in benchmarking hand functions and in the design of hand-related rehabilitation and training programs.
